HYPOTHESIS — How considering academic characteristics alters SES & race effects on BA completion (NLSY79 subset; outcome = years of schooling completed by 1979 as an early-attainment proxy)

"Considering academic characteristics substantially attenuates the estimated effect of family socioeconomic status (SES) on educational attainment and reverses the sign of race effects. Without academic characteristics, a 1-SD increase in a composite SES index (1979 family income, mother's/father's education, professional/managerial father-figure occupation, family size) is associated with ~0.37 SD more schooling (Model B); after adding the ASVAB composite this falls to ~0.17 SD, a 55% attenuation (ASVAB block F=1469, p≈0), and family income, father's education, and occupation each attenuate by 54–84% — indicating that a majority of the SES gradient in schooling operates through academic readiness, with ~65% of the total SES association mediated by test scores (bootstrap CI for indirect effect 0.226–0.256). For race, the raw Black deficit (−0.27 SD vs non-Black/non-Hispanic) is entirely accounted for by family SES (−0.02, n.s.); once academic characteristics are also held constant, Black (+0.05 SD) and particularly Hispanic (+0.25 SD) respondents complete significantly MORE schooling than comparable non-Hispanic white peers — an 'over-performance relative to predicted ability' pattern that is strongest in the upper tail (odds of any college rise to OR≈2.7 for Black and 4.2 for Hispanic after adding ASVAB). The SES gradient is steep among low-ability students (slope 0.27 at ASVAB p10) and near zero among high-ability students (0.06 at p90), while minority advantages persist across the ability distribution (widening with ability for Black students, narrowing for Hispanic students). Adding a measure of school performance (class rank) contributes little beyond ASVAB (SES attenuation 51% vs 55%). Caveats: the only outcome available is attainment by 1979 (cohort aged 14–22), no direct BA-completion variable exists (only n=39 with ≥16 years, too sparse to analyze), and the 1981 ASVAB post-dates the 1979 outcome, so all estimates are associational, not causal."

Supporting tables and the executed script are in the artifacts; the full numeric detail is in analysis_results.txt and results_summary.md.
